posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
Hello everyone,
I've been active here for more than a year now and I feel like I need to focus on other things unrelated to rpg maker or coding in general.
For a bit of history, I've been using RM for... 16 years! (with many interruptions) Starting with VX and then using Ace, I've never really tried to use MV as I was really attached to the 32 tile size and characters from the VX era, and I was away when MZ came out.
I was mostly on the french community when I started and I've played around with many pet projects (my most complete one was the first game I've ever made that I've shared to a friend for their birthday, I've since lost all game data :') ). The last game I worked on, and the only one I released publicly (as poorly balanced demo) progressively became more than a game as I've made a whole TTRPG on its expanded universe, and I even worked on maps of it ahah.
For some time, I was struggling to work on that last project, I've been trying to map a big city for the next part of the game, but its scope was way beyond my motivation.
When BG3 came out, it made me (re)discover CRPGs with tactical battle systems, and it made me want to try to remake my game with a similar battle system.
That's how I came across GTBS which did not fulfil my intention, I've first tried to patch it to fit with my view, but the more I tried to "fix" it, the more I released that I would rather redo it completely, which is why I started my tactical script for ace!
As time had passed between me discovering RM and 2024, the french community was way less active than before, which is one of the reasons why I've joined the english community here. I've been using that time to learn how the engine worked behind the events while learning ruby and comparing it to the programming langages I already knew. I've been writing a few scripts in ruby for the people requesting them, and it was fun.
Now, I'm quite satisfied with my tactical script as I feel like it covers what I wanted (aside from animations), but working on a legacy engine with fewer people does reduce my motivation to continue it as I'm sure not many people will use it.
I also know that working on a personal RPG is very long. I think that I care more about creating stories than making a game around them. And speaking of stories, I have a lot of ideas, but I feel like I lack the life experiences to make meaningful ones to me.
My life and my health also changed and I need to focus on them now instead of procrastinating with RM. So this message is also a way of bringing closure. I will still pop from time to time, especially if I want to improve the things I've posted here or fix bugs I've made :')
With that said, I wish you all a nice journey, be it with or without game making.

posts.author: Solita
posts.body:
Thanks for all you contributed to VXA. Seeing you actively helping people and making more scripts really made me happy as someone who still stays on VXA and owns MV/MZ. Hope your life also improves for the better!
I want to use your battle system for my next game since I'm already too deep in my current project, but I wanted to thank you for making that because GTBS didn't fit what I wanted originally, too.

posts.author: ydoolb
posts.body: Hi! I want to say that even though I didn't know you personally and didn't know you for long, I still feel sad. I hope you'll come back eventually and make a bunch more cool scripts/plugins/some other funny or important things.

posts.author: EntangledPear
posts.body:
Oh no, how did I miss this post! You helped me so much, you will be sorely missed
I hope things will improve for you (I can relate on the health issues). Good luck and do stop by from time to time.

posts.author: Framebitz
posts.body:
Hi Timtrack, Really appreciate you sharing this. 16 years with RPG Maker is amazing!
I get it, sometimes you just need to focus on real life and health first.
Wish you the best moving forward.

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
Heyo... I wanted to say thank you all for your messages, it means a lot to me!
Health and life-related stress are in a better shape currently and honestly brain is still designing stories and some script maintenance/improvements :')
I'm still in a less activity mode and I prefer to keep it that way, though I also did not want to leave no message to your kind words ~
